name: Tom Stalcup
bio: Tom Stalcup is a physicist and entrepreneur who heads an electronics firm making environmental monitoring systems, and previously did research at the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory. He is the Republican nominee for Massachusetts's 4th congressional district, with his campaign based in Brookline.

platform.point: Allow broad Medicare drug price negotiation without artificial limits on which drugs are covered.
Cut federal spending while providing tax relief aimed at households earning under $250,000.
Keep a strong defense, treat war as a last resort, and require Congress to exercise its war powers.
Treat human-caused climate change as real and pursue science-based, innovation-driven solutions that protect economic stability.
Support parental involvement and reduce standardized-testing pressure, favoring more recess and balanced school schedules.

economy.evidence: Wants federal spending cut to essential services with savings returned as tax relief to households earning $250,000 or less.

foreign.evidence: Backs a strong defense but says war must be a last resort with congressional authorization and limits on contractor influence.

energy.evidence: Says human-caused climate change is real and calls for science-based, innovation-led solutions.

notes: Biographical detail comes from his campaign site; an earlier claim about school council service could not be confirmed and was removed.

name: Katherine Clark
current_role: U.S. Representative for MA-5 and House Democratic Whip
bio: Katherine Clark has represented Massachusetts in the U.S. House since winning a 2013 special election and serves as House Democratic Whip. She previously served on the Melrose School Committee and in the Massachusetts House and Senate. She is a lawyer by training.

platform.point: Secure living wages, essential benefits such as paid leave, and union rights for workers.
Treat child care as essential infrastructure backed by federal investment.
Make access to health care a right for everyone.
Protect reproductive freedom along with women's economic power and safety.
Invest in clean energy and environmental justice.
Advance gun violence prevention reforms.

economy.evidence: Campaigns for living wages, paid leave and stronger union rights.

welfare.evidence: Calls health care a right and wants child care treated as federally supported infrastructure.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: pledges to protect reproductive freedom; guns: backs gun violence prevention reforms.

immigration.evidence: Has called for reining in ICE enforcement practices.

energy.evidence: Priorities include investment in clean energy and environmental justice.

education.evidence: Calls for federal investment in public schools and student support services.

name: Dan Koh
current_role: Former White House deputy director of Intergovernmental Affairs
bio: Dan Koh is the Democratic nominee for Massachusetts's 6th district. He was chief of staff to Boston Mayor Marty Walsh, served on the Andover Board of Selectmen, and was chief of staff to Labor Secretary Walsh before a White House intergovernmental affairs role. He holds degrees from Harvard and ran for the 3rd district in 2018.

platform.point: Move to a universal Medicare for All health system.
Oppose ICE and defend the rights of immigrant communities.
Restore abortion rights lost when Roe v. Wade was overturned.
Direct climate resilience resources to North Shore coastal communities.
Lower costs, expand housing and strengthen unions.
Oppose the Trump administration's agenda and protect voting rights.

economy.evidence: Emphasizes affordability, housing and strengthening unions.

welfare.evidence: Supports universal health care through Medicare for All.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion and LGBTQ rights (individual choice) alongside gun safety measures.

immigration.evidence: Opposes ICE and champions immigrant rights.

energy.evidence: Treats climate change as a top priority for coastal communities.

education.evidence: Stresses strong public education as essential to democracy.

notes: The Commons portrait File:Daniel Koh, White House Deputy Cabinet Secretary.jpg is marked public domain but credits a LinkedIn profile as its source, so it was not used.

name: Micah Jones
bio: Micah Q. Jones is the Republican nominee for Massachusetts's 6th district. He is an attorney and a former U.S. Army captain, and his campaign is based in Danvers on the North Shore.

platform.point: Let families deduct child care costs dollar-for-dollar from federal taxes.
Cut permitting delays and duplicative federal review to increase housing supply.
Expand LNG infrastructure, speed nuclear permitting and add renewables while keeping the grid reliable.
Strengthen border enforcement with staffing and technology while clearing legal immigration backlogs.
Set national AI safety and transparency standards while preserving U.S. innovation leadership.
Strengthen congressional oversight and avoid open-ended military commitments.

economy.evidence: Proposes permitting reform, SALT relief and child care tax deductions.

security.evidence: Supports police recruitment and more border enforcement technology, paired with transparency standards.

immigration.evidence: Wants stronger border enforcement and faster adjudication alongside a modernized legal immigration system.

foreign.evidence: Calls for congressional war powers oversight and avoiding open-ended military commitments.

energy.evidence: Backs LNG and nuclear expansion along with renewables, prioritizing affordability and reliability.

tech.evidence: Proposes national AI safety and transparency standards.

name: Ayanna Pressley
bio: Ayanna Pressley has represented Massachusetts's 7th district since 2019 after winning the 2018 Democratic primary against the incumbent. She served on the Boston City Council from 2010 to 2019, the first Black woman elected to that body. She was born in Cincinnati, Ohio.

platform.point: Pursue a just economy, including a federal jobs guarantee and ending the tipped minimum wage.
Treat housing as a human right.
Enact Medicare for All.
Reform the legal system, including ending qualified immunity for police officers.
Take action on climate and environmental challenges.
Cancel federal student loan debt through executive action.

economy.evidence: Supports a federal jobs guarantee and introduced the Be HEARD Act to end the tipped minimum wage.

welfare.evidence: Advocates Medicare for All and expanded Medicaid prenatal and postpartum coverage.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights, marijuana legalization and transgender rights.

security.evidence: Introduced the Ending Qualified Immunity Act to limit legal protections for police.

immigration.evidence: Called for defunding ICE and cosponsored the New Way Forward Act.

foreign.evidence: Voted against Iron Dome funding and criticized the Soleimani strike, though she voted to condemn BDS.

name: Stephen Lynch
bio: Stephen Lynch has represented a Boston-area district in the U.S. House since a 2001 special election. A South Boston native and former ironworker, he led Iron Workers Local 7 before serving in the Massachusetts House and Senate. He serves on the Financial Services and Oversight committees.

platform.point: Pass gun laws such as universal background checks and red flag laws.
Expand jobs and economic opportunity with a focus on working families and labor.
Protect the environment and address climate change.
Maintain strong national security and oversight of military and reconstruction spending.
Support veterans and their benefits.
Protect the U.S. Postal Service.

economy.evidence: Strongly pro-labor, co-founded the Labor and Working Families Caucus, and backed Dodd-Frank and the 2009 stimulus.

welfare.evidence: Voted against the Affordable Care Act in 2010, calling the Senate bill a concession to insurers.

liberty.evidence: Moved from anti-abortion to voting for the Women's Health Protection Act, and supports background checks and red flag gun laws.

foreign.evidence: Voted for the 2002 Iraq War authorization and supported Afghanistan war funding.

education.evidence: Said in 2016 he would vote for the Massachusetts ballot question to expand charter schools.

notes: Education score is new and rests on a single 2016 statement supporting charter school expansion.

name: Robert Burke
bio: Robert (Rob) Burke is the Republican nominee for Massachusetts's 8th congressional district. His campaign focuses on election integrity, affordability, immigration and public safety.

platform.point: Require voter ID and citizenship verification to secure elections.
Cut taxes, restore manufacturing, reduce inflation and make homeownership attainable.
Pause immigration entirely while programs are reevaluated.
Give law enforcement more resources to reduce crime.
Shift toward individually purchased catastrophic insurance with wellness incentives.
Increase judicial accountability and prevent politicized prosecutions.

economy.evidence: Calls for tax cuts and reducing inflation to restore manufacturing.

welfare.evidence: Favors personal catastrophic insurance plans over broad public coverage.

security.evidence: Wants more law enforcement resources to fight crime.

immigration.evidence: Proposes a comprehensive pause on immigration.

foreign.evidence: Opposes what the campaign describes as global giveaways of U.S. money.

notes: The campaign site gives no biography or career details.

name: Bill Keating
bio: Bill Keating has served in the U.S. House since 2011 and represents the South Coast and Cape Cod district. He previously served in the Massachusetts House and Senate and was Norfolk County District Attorney from 1999 to 2011. He sits on the Armed Services and Foreign Affairs committees and is ranking member of the Europe subcommittee.

platform.point: Lead on European security and support for Ukraine through the Foreign Affairs Europe subcommittee.
Close the loophole that lets people on FBI watchlists buy firearms.
Back labor-supported legislation on wages and workers' rights.
Press for safety oversight of nuclear plants such as Pilgrim Station.

liberty.evidence: Votes for abortion rights and LGBTQ protections and supports tighter gun purchase rules.

foreign.evidence: Ranking member of the Europe subcommittee and active in the Ukraine Caucus.

faith.evidence: Cosponsored the Equitable Access to Care and Health Act creating religious exemptions under the ACA.

notes: No campaign website was identified; the faith score rests on a single cosponsorship.

name: Tyler MacAllister
current_role: Mattapoisett Select Board member and fisherman
bio: Tyler MacAllister is the Republican nominee for Massachusetts's 9th district. He has lived in Mattapoisett since 2001, has served five terms on its Select Board and has fished local waters for more than 40 years.

platform.point: Protect the fishing fleet and waterfront with science-based policy.
Bring down grocery, fuel and housing costs.
Support local law enforcement and community safety.
Cut waste and excess spending in Washington.
Honor commitments to veterans and protect seniors' earned benefits.
Balance coastal preservation with practical approaches, including scrutiny of offshore wind projects.

security.evidence: Lists support for law enforcement and community safety as a priority.

energy.evidence: Raises environmental and fishing-industry concerns about offshore wind projects such as Vineyard Wind.

notes: The energy score rests on his campaign account of a trip to inspect the Vineyard Wind turbines rather than a stated policy.

name: Jack Bergman
bio: Jack Bergman has represented Michigan's 1st district since 2017. He is a retired Marine Corps lieutenant general who commanded Marine Forces Reserve, a naval aviator and a former airline pilot. Born in Minnesota, he lives in Watersmeet and serves on the Armed Services, Budget and Veterans' Affairs committees.

platform.point: Require proof of citizenship to vote through the SAVE Act.
Maintain military readiness and a strong defense through the Armed Services Committee.
Improve veterans' health care and disability assistance.
Pursue a balanced budget and restrain federal spending.
Roll back federal energy regulations such as EPA methane emissions rules.

economy.evidence: Supports a balanced budget and voted against COVID relief spending.

welfare.evidence: Voted to repeal the Affordable Care Act in 2017.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion and voted against the Respect for Marriage Act, while supporting gun rights.

immigration.evidence: Backs strict border enforcement and cosponsored the SAVE Act.

foreign.evidence: Supports a strong military and strong backing for Israel.

energy.evidence: Voted in 2025 against EPA methane emissions rules and supports expanded drilling.

education.evidence: Supports school vouchers and school choice.

faith.evidence: Has described Bible-based values as guiding his public positions.

notes: Several scores rely on OnTheIssues summaries that were not re-checked in this pass.

name: Callie Barr
bio: Callie Barr is the Democratic nominee for Michigan's 1st district. She grew up in Traverse City and Cheboygan and worked as a teacher and veterans advocate before becoming an attorney. Her campaign biography describes her as a military spouse.

platform.point: Unlock federal funding for local affordable homebuilding and reform zoning to add supply.
Make the wealthy pay their fair share, protect Social Security and expand rural broadband.
End tariffs that hurt farmers, support food banks and reverse SNAP cuts.
Protect rural hospitals and Medicaid, extend ACA subsidies and lower drug costs.
Fully fund the VA.

economy.evidence: Calls for higher taxes on the wealthy, lifting the Social Security cap and passing the PRO Act.

welfare.evidence: Wants to protect Medicaid, extend ACA subsidies, add a public option and reverse SNAP cuts.

notes: No campaign social media accounts were found on the campaign site.

name: Arnett Satterla
bio: Arnett Satterla is the Libertarian Party nominee for Michigan's 1st congressional district.
notes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia profile or public statements could be found.
